purpose: Miglustat is used to treat a rare inherited condition called Gaucher disease, specifically the type that mainly affects your organs rather than your brain and bones. It may also be used for another rare condition called Niemann-Pick type C disease. It helps manage symptoms when other treatments are not suitable for you.
how_it_works: Your body normally uses an enzyme to break down certain fatty substances. In Gaucher disease, that enzyme does not work properly, so fatty material builds up in your organs like the spleen and liver. Miglustat works by slowing down how much of that fatty substance your body makes in the first place, so less builds up over time — think of it like turning down the production line when you cannot clear the backlog fast enough.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea and stomach cramps are very common, especially when you first start the medication. You may also notice weight loss, gas, bloating, or feeling shaky or unsteady on your feet. Some people experience tingling or numbness in the hands and feet. These effects often improve over time.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — this medicine must NOT be used during pregnancy as it can harm the baby. Both men and women should use reliable contraception during treatment and for a period after stopping. If you notice worsening tremors, balance problems, or vision changes, contact your doctor right away. Regular nerve and coordination check-ups are recommended while on this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is one 100 mg capsule taken three times a day by mouth, roughly every 8 hours. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose to help reduce stomach side effects and adjust as needed. Always take it as directed and do not skip doses without talking to your doctor first.
